content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: outage IVR message, 20% chat deflection, callbacks and overtime for 38 payments agents 13:30-14:30. Predicted 84.2% service level for ₹15,291, with no policy breaches.","why":"The spike is driven by the P1 UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls were 90% over forecast at 10:30 and upi_payment_failed calls ran 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so this is a demand problem. R1 tackles it from both sides: the IVR outage message, chat deflection and callbacks cut payments demand, and concentrated overtime adds capacity. It is predicted to reach 84.2% overall (payments 80.4%, general 90.3%), with abandons at 3.7%. It is the cheapest option that meets the 80% target without breaking policy. It leaves general's agents and breaks untouched.","trade_offs":["Doing nothing (P0) costs ₹9,399 but leaves service level at 69.7%, with payments at 61.2% and abandons at 10.1%.","The cheaper plans P1, P2 and P4 (₹9,399–₹11,559) all miss the target (75.5–78.7%). They also break policy: 15 agents would have more than one break delayed, and moving agents would pull general down to 53–64%, below its 70% floor.","P3 reaches a similar 84.1% but costs ₹540 more (₹15,831). It still breaches the break and general-floor rules.","R2 spreads overtime over a longer window (13:30-15:00) at ₹15,831 but only reaches 82.4%, with payments at 77.8%. R1 does better for less."],"watch":"R1 depends on enough agents accepting overtime: it needs 38 payments agents for 13:30-14:30. Track uptake early. Also watch payments service level after 14:30, when the overtime ends but the outage may not. If the UPI incident runs past 15:00, or volumes keep climbing, revisit the plan."}
